_comment: Metals & Non-metals WS1 — no printed key; all answers DERIVED for review.

1.reason: Carbon is a food constituent; CO is toxic/suffocating, CO2 causes global warming.

2.reason: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature.

3.reason: Non-metals are below hydrogen in reactivity, so cannot displace H from acids.

4.reason: C2H5OH (ethanol) and glucose are covalent/molecular, non-electrolytes; II and III.

5.reason: Mg is the central metal of chlorophyll in plants.

6.reason: Graphite is the non-metal that conducts electricity due to free electrons.

8.reason: Cu (more reactive than Ag) displaces silver from AgNO3 solution.

9.reason: Al used in thermite; Al2O3 is amphoteric.

10.reason: Hydraulic washing (density, true) and carbonate calcination in absence of air (true); statements 2 (froth=sulphide not magnetic) and 3 (reactive-metal oxides not reduced by heat alone) are false.

11.reason: CaF, NaCl, MgO are ionic (A,B,C); CO2 is covalent.

12.reason: Carbon removes oxygen from Fe2O3, so C is the reducing agent.

13.reason: Pt (platinum), least reactive noble metal, occurs free; CO is not an element.

14.reason: Ca reacts less violently with water (C) and H2 bubbles stick to its surface (D).

16.reason: Statement 1 is correct (true). Incorrect: 2 (C cannot reduce Na/Mg oxides), 3 (NaCl conducts only in molten/aqueous, not solid), 4 (K/Ca/Mg are reactive, found combined). So incorrect = II, III and IV.

17.reason: Zinc is malleable (metal); the rest are non-metals.

18.reason: N (nitrogen) is the non-metal; Al, Fe, Zn are metals.

19.reason: HCl and CCl4 are covalent (not ionic); ii and iii.

20.reason: Ionic compound Z has HIGH melting point, so 'low melting point' is the property NOT shown.

22.reason: Bromine is the liquid non-metal at room temperature.

23.reason: Gallium (mp ~30 C) melts on the warm palm.

24.reason: PVC is the common insulating coating for wires.

25.reason: Both statements true and statement 2 (oxides easier to reduce) is the correct explanation of statement 1 (sulphides/carbonates converted to oxides first).

26.reason: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of metals/metal-nonmetal.

27.reason: Ag is least reactive, so it is displaced from its salt solution by the other three (Mg, Cu, Zn).

28.reason: Non-metals typically have 5, 6 or 7 valence electrons.

29.reason: Incorrect match: electric wires use Copper, not Magnesium.

30.reason: Mercury (metal) and Bromine (non-metal) are both liquid at room temperature.

32.reason: Fe (iron) reacts only with steam, not cold/hot water, giving H2.

33.reason: Amphoteric oxides react with both acid and base to give salt and water.

34.reason: Activity series Ca>Mg>Al: Mg is below Ca and above Al (true). A is false: Cu is below lead (Pb above H, Cu below H).

35.reason: Lithium has the lowest density (0.53 g/cc) among the options.

37.reason: Au and Ag (and Cu) occur native; among options Au(ii) and Ag(iv).

38.reason: Water, dilute H2SO4, and ethanol (with Na) all liberate H2 with suitable metals, so All of these.

39.reason: Green coating on copper in air is basic copper carbonate, CuCO3 (patina).

40.reason: Calcium forms CaO (high mp) which is soluble in water giving Ca(OH)2.

43.reason: Aluminium foil is malleable, so it can be made into thin wrapping sheets.

45.reason: Sodium is stored in kerosene to prevent reaction with air/moisture.

46.reason: Lead is malleable but a poor conductor of electricity.

47.reason: Aqua regia = Conc.HCl : Conc.HNO3 in 3:1 ratio.

48.reason: Fe displaces Cu; blue CuSO4 turns to green FeSO4.

49.reason: Incorrect: Solder = lead + tin (not zinc+tin, iii) and Bronze = copper + tin (not Al+Cu, v). So (iii) and (v).

50.reason: Melting point of NaCl is 1074 K (801 C) = option C. (Option C text corrected from a misread 1474 to 1074.)

51.reason: Silver tarnishes black forming Ag2S with H2S in air.

52.reason: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it cannot be used to coat food cans (would react with food).

53.reason: Al is oxidized to Al2O3, so Al is the reducing agent.

54.reason: Cu is below H in reactivity series; no reaction with dilute H2SO4.

55.reason: Fe does not react with cold or hot water (only steam); among the options Fe.

58.reason: Drawing metals into wires is ductility.

60.reason: Roasting heats sulphide ore in the presence of (excess) air.

61.reason: Iron with prolonged steam gives Fe3O4 (magnetic iron oxide).

63.reason: A (Z=11, Na) and B (Z=12, Mg) are both metals.

64.reason: Basic lining of a furnace uses calcined dolomite (CaO.MgO), a basic refractory.

65.reason: Steel contains carbon (a non-metal) with iron.

66.reason: Anhydrous CaCl2 is a drying agent; it absorbs moisture.

67.reason: Phosphorus (white) is stored in water; sodium is stored in kerosene.

68.reason: Snack/dried-fruit bags are flushed with inert nitrogen gas.

69.reason: Copper and silver occur in both native (free) and combined (ore) states; gold/platinum are essentially free-state.

70.reason: Green patina on copper is basic copper carbonate.

71.reason: Fountain experiment shows the high solubility of NH3 in water.

72.reason: Lead (Pb) is bluish-grey, not silvery white; Al, Sn and Ag are silvery white.

73.reason: Copper is below H and does not react readily with water; Na, K react vigorously.

75.reason: The ringing of a bell is due to the sonorous property of metals.

41.reason: Heating PbO with a reducing agent Y (carbon): PbO + C -> Pb + CO. Residue = shiny molten globules of lead (Pb); Y = carbon (C); a substance that can replace carbon as the reducing agent is a metal more reactive than Pb, e.g. magnesium (Mg). Only option B names Pb, C and Mg together.
